hero.lead: A nation of 36,000 on coral atolls in the North Pacific, with $2.3 billion of United States economic assistance through 2043 under its renewed Compact and $60 million from the World Bank for renewable power.

register.name: Trust Fund for the People of the Marshall Islands
register.detail: The compact trust fund · balance $1.6 billion at 30 November 2025, according to its Trust Fund Committee · US contributions of $700 million by 2027 · first US deposit of $200 million, July 2024
register.note: US contributions to reach $700 million by 2027, in annual payments
register.text: The trust fund of the Marshall Islands under the Compact of Free Association, which the US Department of the Interior describes as a source of revenue for the needs of the Marshallese people. The United States will make $700 million available to it by 2027; its revenue bears on the public finances that pay for schools, clinics and services.

register.name: Fiscal Management and Disaster and Climate Resilience DPO with a Cat DDO
register.detail: World Bank · approved 19 July 2024 · additional US$9 million, June 2026 · US$30 million in all · US$12 million of contingent financing for an eligible catastrophe · P504373
register.note: Additional US$9 million for the energy crisis, June 2026
register.text: Budget support for the Marshall Islands with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option, contingent financing that is released when an eligible disaster strikes. In June 2026 the World Bank added US$9 million to help the nation respond to sharply higher energy costs for families, businesses, public services and the national budget.

register.name: Urban Resilience Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · additional financing · announced in Majuro, 8 April 2026 · amount not stated in the release
register.note: A significant share of the support for Majuro
register.text: Additional financing to scale up urban resilience investments in public buildings and spaces, strengthen national disaster preparedness and response systems, support building code implementation and deliver resilient, multi-purpose emergency management facilities. Its civil works support local jobs and protect communities against climate and disaster risks, which bears on the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Strengthening Public Financial Management II
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) grant · announced in Majuro, 8 August 2025 · accounting, internal audit and procurement · digital financial systems · public access to budget and procurement records
register.note: Includes support toward Green Climate Fund accreditation requirements
register.text: An IDA grant to train and certify public finance staff, particularly women, in accounting, internal audit and procurement, and to expand digital government financial systems and public access to budget and procurement records. Sound management of public money bears on the public finances that pay for the seven standards.

register.name: Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) grant E331-MH of SDR 45.6 million · approved 24 September 2024 · financing agreement signed 22 October 2024 · closing 30 September 2030 · mini-grid contract awarded August 2026
register.note: Four new solar mini-grids on Arno Atoll; solar and batteries for Jabor, Wotje and Rongrong
register.text: An IDA grant to increase renewable energy generation and improve the reliability and quality of electricity service in targeted main and outer islands. In August 2026 the Marshalls Energy Company awarded the contract for four new solar mini-grids on Arno Atoll and the solar and battery hybridisation of three diesel systems at Jabor, Wotje and Rongrong, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Pacific Resilience Project II, additional financing
register.text: Additional financing for the Pacific Resilience Project II in the Marshall Islands, for coastal protection and preparedness. Protection against storm surge and rising seas bears on the shelter standard of a nation of low-lying atolls.

register.name: Pacific Disaster Resilience Program, phase 5: contingent disaster financing
register.detail: ADB · released 11 November 2026 · state of disaster for El Niño and dengue fever declared 8 October 2026 · phase 5 approved June 2024
register.note: Phase 5 includes policy-based grants to the Marshall Islands
register.text: Contingent disaster financing released by ADB to support the response of the Marshall Islands to El Niño-related hazards and a dengue fever outbreak affecting Majuro and Ebeye. The release supports the response to the outbreak, which bears on the health standard.

register.name: Public Sector Reform Program, subprogram 1
register.detail: ADB grant · approved 5 November 2026 · includes $6.7 million of additional funding · after a state of economic emergency declared in March 2026
register.note: Aims to bring subsidies and transfers to state-owned companies from 6.2% of GDP (2020 to 2024 average) to 3% by 2028
register.text: A grant for the first phase of a programme of tax, spending and public-service reforms, which helps the government meet increased financing needs as the Middle East conflict raises fuel and food costs. It supports the public finances as a whole.

register.name: Energy Transition Project
register.detail: ADB grant · 2024 · effective 20 January 2025 · completion targeted for December 2028 · a new Majuro substation and about 10 miles of distribution lines
register.note: The Marshalls Energy Company gives the project as $17 million
register.text: An ADB grant to enhance energy distribution in Majuro, support low-carbon renewable installations and strengthen resilience on smaller islands, with early deployment of ocean and wind energy and a new sector law. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Women and Youth Skills, Empowerment, and Resilience Project
register.detail: ADB grant from the Asian Development Fund · announced 7 November 2024 · Majuro and the College of the Marshall Islands
register.note: Includes a disability-accessible centre and a childcare centre
register.text: An ADB grant to renovate a Majuro facility for training and support services for women and youth, build a disability-accessible two-storey centre, and build a childcare centre and a training and study facility at the College of the Marshall Islands. Informal training in financial literacy, bookkeeping and computer skills serves the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Integrated Urban Services and Resilience Improvement Project
register.detail: ADB grant from the Asian Development Fund · signed in Majuro, 24 September 2024 · Project 52034-001 · Majuro and Ebeye
register.note: Water, sanitation and waste in Majuro; climate-resilient oceanside roads in Ebeye
register.text: An ADB grant to upgrade facilities and systems for water, sanitation and waste management in Majuro and build the capacity of its urban service providers, and to rehabilitate oceanside roads in Ebeye with climate-resilient materials and better drainage. It serves the water and shelter standards and resilience to drought, storm surge and sea-level rise.

register.name: Public financial management reforms, additional financing
register.detail: ADB grant from the Asian Development Fund · 2024 · Ministry of Finance
register.note: As listed on ADB’s country page
register.text: Additional ADB grant financing to strengthen the public financial management reforms of the Ministry of Finance. It supports the public finances as a whole.

register.name: Project for Strengthening Local Food Supply
register.detail: Grant aid of Japan, with IOM · exchange of notes signed in Majuro, 24 February 2026 · up to ¥203 million, about US$1.3 million · two years
register.note: Community and school programmes for climate-resilient food
register.text: Japanese grant aid, carried out with the International Organization for Migration, for community and school programmes that build climate-resilient food systems and teach sustainable farming and healthy cooking with local ingredients. It aims to raise local food production and reduce dependence on imported food, which serves the food standard.

register.name: Seed contribution to the Marshall Islands Resilience and Adaptation Trust Fund
register.note: Seed funding for a newly established national trust fund
register.text: Australian seed funding of US$2 million, from 2026 to 2028, for the newly established Marshall Islands Resilience and Adaptation Trust Fund (MIRA). A national fund for resilience and adaptation bears on the shelter and water standards of atolls that rise only a little above the sea.

register.name: Compact of Free Association, economic assistance
register.detail: United States · Compact of Free Association Amendments Act of 2024 (P.L. 118-42) · signed into law 9 March 2024 · through FY2043 · sector grants of $51 million in FY2025 · $700 million to the trust fund by 2027
register.note: Sector grants are 53 percent of the total
register.text: Twenty years of US assistance to the Marshall Islands under the renewed Compact, in sector grants and contributions to the nation’s trust fund. The US Government Accountability Office reports, in May 2026, that education and health remain the priorities, which serves those two standards.

register.name: WASH in Schools Promoting Inclusion Resilience and Equity (WinSPIRE)
register.note: Water, sanitation and hygiene in schools
register.text: An Australian programme, delivered with UNICEF, for water, sanitation and hygiene in the schools of the Marshall Islands. It serves the water standard for children.

items.text: Marshallese abroad, many in the United States, send home almost a quarter of the economy.

items.text: Coconut groves and atoll forest across half the land.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2018
items.text: Bikini Atoll, wrecks and lagoons: a small visitor economy with a unique history.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 33.9% are under fifteen: a young nation that can live and work in the United States under the Compact.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: Elefa Handicrafts
items.text: A Marshallese handicraft business that exports bags and other products woven from the leaves of young coconut trees and the pandanus tree to Japan, the Cook Islands, Samoa and the United States, giving single mothers in Majuro the means to make a living, with weavers on the outer islands supplying some products.
